title: Toronto police officer could face life in prison after man's death following suicide attempt
subtitle: The provincial SIU charged Const. Kyle Upjohn with criminal negligence causing death and failing to provide the necessities of life after a five-month investigation
article: A Toronto police officer could be facing life in prison after he was charged for his role in what began as a suicide attempt.

The provincial Special Investigations Unit (SIU) charged Const. Kyle Upjohn with criminal negligence causing death and failing to provide the necessities of life Thursday after a five-month investigation into a February incident in High Park.
According to the SIU, a man sought the help of a police officer in the park at about 2 p.m. on Feb. 2 in relation to a suicide attempt by another man. By 3:30 p.m., a suicidal 19-year-old was dead.
The SIU did not release any further details about the case.
According to the Ontario government's sunshine list, a Const. Kyle Upjohn of the Toronto Police Service earned $106,000 last year.
The maximum penalty for criminal negligence causing death is life in prison. Upjohn is due to appear at Toronto's Old City Hall courthouse on Aug. 4.
